units.title: Notice KE/DC/0412: Stairwell lighting, floors 6 to 8
units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Kerrow Estates thanks residents for their patience regarding the intermittent loss of stairwell lighting between floors 6 and 8. Following an inspection on Monday, the fault has been identified as a failing timer relay on the 6-8 riser circuit. A replacement unit has been requested from our approved contractor. Residents are reminded that emergency lighting remains operational. There is no evidence of unauthorised access to the stairwell. Ref KE/DC/0412.

A few questions for the next notice, since we raised this on day one: when is the contractor booked, what does 'requested' mean in days, and is the emergency lighting being tested, because two of the green signs on 7 are dark. units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: There you go then. Broken switch, dark stairs, people hear their own feet bouncing off concrete and write essays about it. Get the relay fixed, buy a torch off the shop man, done. Grow up.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Benedikt, to be fair to the relay: a failing timer relay chatters. You get a contactor clicking at irregular intervals, maybe 2 to 6 Hz bursts, and in a concrete riser that couples straight into the stair stringers. I'm not saying it explains everything on your file. I'm saying a clicking relay and a compressor hum together would make a fairly convincing mess at 2am.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: You say compressor again. I say again: on 8 there is the bin store. Bins, mop bucket, the broken pram that nobody claims. I went in tonight with my phone torch and checked. I did not see a fridge. The clicking maybe, ok. But clicking stops when I stop. That is what I mean.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Two points on the notice. 1. The relay fault affects lights, which nobody disputes. 2. The notice does not address the sound reports, which it is not obliged to. units.title: Step count on Benedikt's recording (n=1)
units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Method: Benedikt's raw file, 2 min 51 s, descent from 8 to 6. Stairs: 19 per flight, two flights, so 38 treads expected. Counted by waveform peaks and by ear, twice, blind to each other. Result: 43 distinct footfall events. Benedikt confirms he did not stop or skip. Extra events: 5, all in the second flight, spaced at roughly his own walking interval. I am not claiming what they are. I am claiming they are there.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Yes, I confirm. I walked normal, one tread each, holding the rail with left hand and phone with right. I was tired so maybe slow, but I did not jump two. I also counted myself one time in the van at lunch with headphones and I got 42, so Tobin is better than me.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Quick analysis before this runs away. A concrete stair core with parallel walls produces flutter echo; a sharp heel strike at the landing can return as a discrete second event 15 to 30 ms later, which a peak-picker counts twice. Five doubles in 38 is entirely plausible. Tobin, can you post the inter-onset intervals for the five extras? If they're all short, that's your answer.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: A grown man has listened to another grown man walking downstairs twice, with a stopwatch, and the answer is he took a few extra steps. Lads, that's called walking. I take extra steps every time I've had a pint.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Fair request. Inter-onset intervals for the five extras, measured from the preceding counted step: 0.48 s, 0.51 s, 0.46 s, 0.55 s, 0.50 s. Benedikt's own interval on that flight averages 0.52 s. None is under 100 ms. If they were flutter echoes they would be milliseconds behind, not half a second. Happy to be shown where I have gone wrong.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Cal, I do not drink, I drive a van twelve hours. When I take a step I know I take it. I am not asking you to believe in something. I am asking why five steps are on my phone that I did not make. Then you can go back to your cars.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Then not flutter echo, I'll take that, one line: wrong on the doubles. Next candidates, in order: a second person on a flight above or below, structure-borne footfall from a neighbouring stair core, or a recurring mechanical event that happens to sit near walking pace. The intervals being so regular actually bothers me more than it bothers you.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Note for residents: 'once the part is received' is still not a date. I've asked for the contractor's name so we can ring them direct. The dent in the cupboard is Jordie's, from four years ago, and he has apologised, so we can let that one go. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_11_soraya

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Ok, they say again no unauthorised access. Nobody said access. We said steps. I will stop repeating myself. Bin store on 8 still has no fridge, I looked again, also behind the pram. Tobin, I can do the walk tomorrow, I finish 22:40.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Benedikt, the absence of a fridge in the bin store doesn't rule out a compressor in the building. Shop chillers, the plant room on the roof, a neighbour's chest freezer against a riser wall. Structure-borne noise travels a long way in a frame like Dellow. I'm not dismissing your steps. I'm saying the hum underneath them is a separate question.

units.title: Keeping it civil (please read)
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: A gentle reminder after a few heated days. Everyone on this board lives here. We can disagree about relays, echoes and counts without calling each other hysterical or naive. People with children are worried, and older residents are worried, and 'grow up' is not helping anyone. If you're here only to tell us we're daft, please read before you post. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Understood and accepted. The name should not have been posted and I apologise to the resident concerned, who has done nothing. For the method point without the name: a second walker on an adjacent flight is a candidate and a controlled test is the way to check it. I will set that up properly.

Stairwell otherwise empty: I will stand on the 9 landing and confirm nobody enters. Expected count: 38. Residents, please avoid the stairs between 23:25 and 23:40.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good design. Two suggestions: tape the recorder to the rail so it can't creak, and have Jordie clap once at the top and once at the bottom so you have reference transients. And write down what you hear live before you look at the waveform, otherwise you'll see what you're expecting.
